translation.text: Have hope, righteous ones,[a] for sinners will soon perish before you.[b] And authority over them will be yours, as you have wished.[c]

footnotes.text: This follows the selected main text of Charles1906, printed200, not a newly inspected manuscript. The righteous address is asterisk-marked. His apparatus15–20 reports an alternative opening, omissions and variations in the authority and final relational phrases. These reported alternatives are not silently substituted into the selected main line.

The verb belongs to the perishing/destruction family and here has the reflexive/intransitive form. No agent of destruction is stated. Before you renders the source expression literally from before your plural presence; soon renders its quickly/soon adverb. This assurance supplies no calendar date.

Authority is the singular subject of will be, with for you and over them; the last verb is a second-person plural perfect, hence as you have wished. Charles reports an alternative authority form at17, omission of for you by g,u at18, over you in u at19, and variations or omission of the final comparison at20. These are his apparatus reports, not independent manuscript checks.
